judge_notes: 'Of' and 'About' are distinct prepositional relations (e.g. capital of France vs capital about France) not generally interchangeable, and the example doesn't even illustrate this swap.

"Of" is a broad, multi-sense relator (possession, composition, part-whole, topic) while "About" only marks topic, so collapsing them is unsafe outside this narrow relational-noun "history of/about X" construction.

'Of' spans many relations (possession, part-whole, role) while 'About' specifically marks topic/aboutness, so they are not general synonyms (e.g. 'Prime Minister of Canada' cannot become 'Prime Minister About Canada').
'rate of flow' and 'flow rate' are the same compound noun in N-of-N vs N-N word order, true synonyms.
"rate of flow" and "flow rate" are the same technical term merely reordered, fully interchangeable in all contexts.
"rate of flow" and "flow rate" are the identical technical noun phrase in prepositional vs. compound word order, true synonyms.
'Train station' and 'railway station' denote the same real-world facility class, genuine synonyms.
"Train station" and "railway station" are dialectal (AmE/BrE) synonyms denoting the identical class of passenger rail facility.
'Train station' and 'railway station' denote the identical class of facility, differing only by US/UK dialect preference.

orchestrate implies skillful/covert coordination of many parts while direct is the neutral term for helming a production, and they diverge sharply outside this scenario (e.g. 'orchestrate a takeover' vs 'direct a takeover', 'direct traffic' vs 'orchestrate traffic').

orchestrate implies skillful coordination of complex/disparate elements and is not a general synonym for the neutral professional-role verb direct (e.g. direct traffic, direct a letter), only a loose metaphorical match here.
"orchestrate" implies elaborate/covert coordination of many parts (e.g. "orchestrate a scandal") while "direct" is the neutral formal production-role verb, not general synonyms.
'Divide' carries senses (arithmetic division, splitting opinion/a group) that 'separate' lacks, so the lemma classes aren't fully interchangeable.
"Divide" and "separate" overlap for the splitting-into-parts sense used here but diverge elsewhere (mathematical division, isolating one item from a group), so the class-level swap fails in general.
'Divide' and 'separate' overlap only in the 'split into parts' sense but diverge elsewhere (e.g. couples 'separate' but don't 'divide'; arithmetic division isn't separation), so not general synonyms.

propose carries a stronger/more formal commitment to putting forward a claim or plan than the more tentative suggest, and the two diverge outside this scenario (e.g. 'propose marriage' vs 'suggest marriage', 'propose a bill' vs 'suggest a bill').
propose entails a more formal, committed act of putting an idea forward for consideration while suggest is more tentative/less committal, a strength/formality scale shift not a true synonym pair.

"propose" carries a stronger, more formal/decisive commitment (e.g. propose marriage, propose a formal plan) than the tentative, hinting "suggest", so the swap loses that register/strength distinction.
Patient (undergoes change of state) and Theme (unaffected/located/described entity) are distinct thematic roles in general, even though this particular cancel-event filler is a borderline case.

Patient (entity undergoing a change of state) and Theme (entity located/moved, not necessarily changed) are distinct thematic roles that only coincide for "cancel"; merging them loses the affectedness distinction generally.
Patient (undergoer of a change of state, e.g. cancellation) and Theme (entity located/described without necessarily changing state) are distinct thematic roles, not freely interchangeable.
